main_text.p: defunt ? at tefte{y} y Lib.5. ca.14. Sozomeno [tanta erat eorum multitudo, ut magiltratus cuiusque civitatis ægrè eorum calculum subducere, & in tabulas referre potuerint. Et in ipso Exercitu, tantus numerus, ut cùm post Iuliani mortem, Iouianus Christianus, Christianus, violenter à militibus ad imperium raptus, illis imperare recusasset, qui à fide sua alieni essent: milites pœnè omnes, acri voce, velut ex compofito, Cuspin. in Iuliano. se quoque Christum colere acclamarent. Num ductoribus vobis opus est? at habetis Iovianum, Valentinianum, Valentem, qui postea sunt imperij gubernaculis potiti, & denique Artemium Ægypti Præfectum sub ipso Constantino Artis Militaris peritia, celebrem: Vobis interea idem animus, eadem mens, quæ Orat.2. in Iulianum Gregorio Nazianzeno. De his Iuliani temporibus loquens, [nobis quibus nulla alia arma, nec muri, nec præsidia, præter spem in Deum reliqua erant, quem tandem alium, aut precum auditorem aut minarum depulsorem habituri eramus quàm Deum? Quorum enim extentæ inter precandum manus flammas extinguunt, feras consopiuunt, gladiorū acię re-

page.notes: The marginal note reads "y Lib.5. ca.14.", with the reference mark y. Mark y in the text stands after "tefte". The text is cut off at the foot of this part and continues on the second image. The s of "Sozomeno" line 1 is a plain s, and some words are read from the image with a spot of ink near "magiltratus" that is not a letter. Reference marks in the text are a small z before "se quoque" and a small a before "Gregorio"; the margin notes carry the same letters. The opening bracket "[" before "nobis" is printed and kept. The line "gladiorū acię" ends with a printed tilde over the e; read as ę with [?]. "re-" below the last line is the catchword. Show-through marks in the right margin are not transcribed. Printing errors left as printed: "Iouianum" is read as Iovianum by the u/v rule.
